newsitem.title: GERMANY: U-Freight expansion plans in growing Chinese marke.
newsitem.headline: U-Freight expansion plans in growing Chinese marke.

text.p: International freight forwarder U-Freight said it will expand its presence in China this year as the giant market continued to grow strongly.
Its China Express subsidiary would open a new freight hub at Dalian airport as part of a five million dollar investment programme at the airport, it said.
U-Freight opened a $1.8 million Shanghai complex with a 4,200 sq m warehouse and 850 sq m of offices last year.

Speaking at the recent U-Freight European sales meeting in Munich, Gene Boyer, U-Freight managing director Americas & Europe, said: "The Chinese market is huge but it cannot be quantified at the moment."
"Everyone says they are in China but not everyone has the correct licence. U-Freight does," he added.
U-Freight had moved hundreds of tonnes in recent years between Brazil and China for Volkswagen AG, Boyer noted.
N.S. Cheong, U-Freight owner and director, said U-Freight would open an office at Hong Kong's new Chep Lap Kok airport when it opened in April 1998.

He forecast Hong Kong would continue to be the freight hub for southern China since up to 90 percent of air freight passing through Hong Kong was going to or from China. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
